entities.summary:
Leontius was a general of the Eastern Roman Empire and claimant to the throne who led a rebellion against Emperor Zeno in 484–488.




Leontius was the son of the Eastern Roman general and senator, Leontius, and likely had a close relationship with the Emperor's family.




The rebellion was sparked by a combination of economic hardship, military defeats, and personal grievances against Emperor Zeno, who was seen as out of touch with the needs of the Eastern provinces.








Leontius's rebellion was ultimately unsuccessful, and he was defeated and executed by the Emperor's forces in 488 CE.








His legacy as a military leader and would-be emperor has been largely forgotten in modern historiography, but his rebellion remains an important example of the tensions and conflicts within the Eastern Roman Empire during its final centuries.
